subject: Edge VPN & peering performance qualification — post-demo recap
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Sam Liao <sam.liao@finventory.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Edge VPN & peering performance qualification — post-demo recap

Sam — thanks again for the demo time this morning. Quick recap and the concrete asks we promised to send so your infra team can validate feasibility.

High-level goal: validate our Private (VPC) deployment meets Finventory's streaming & SLO needs for production inference. We discussed peering vs VPN and a hybrid fallback; below are the performance targets and the items we need to confirm before a full validation run.

SLO / perf targets (customer ask):
- E2E streaming: initial-token latency (when streaming starts) p95 <= 250 ms, p99 <= 500 ms
- Per-request tail (full response) p95 <= 750 ms for medium-length (<= 1024 tokens) responses
- Sustained concurrency: 200 concurrent streaming sessions, with burst up to 500 for <= 10m windows
- Sustained throughput: ~60 req/s aggregate to start (we can scale down/up during validation)
- Network tolerance: packet loss <= 0.1%, jitter <= 10 ms on the path to the inference nodes
- VPN/peering throughput: baseline 1 Gbps available for test (customer prefers dedicated egress NAT or static IP)

Items we need from your side before we schedule end-to-end tests:
1) Network diagram for the path (Finventory VPC -> peering / VPN -> Redwood Private nodes)
2) VPN details: MTU, cipher (IPsec), whether BGP is used for dynamic routes, any tunnel limits (concurrency/throughput)
3) Firewall/NACL rules and any proxies that may terminate or buffer streaming sockets
4) Egress requirements: whether a static NAT IP is required or if outbound is through your gateway (affects allowlists)
5) Ops contact for a short hands-on window (we'd like one on-call engineer present during the test)
6) Preferred test windows (we propose next Thu/Fri morning Pacific; please confirm)

Attachments: finventory_vpn_requirements.xlsx (initial checklist) and rdw-test-plan.pdf (our proposed perf harness and metrics we emit).

Next steps: if you can send the items above, we will provision a small dedicated test pool and share an exact runbook and a short set of synthetic tests (streaming + small-burst concurrency). Our DevOps engineer (Dev Patel) will coordinate the test harness.

Thanks — want to get this scheduled quickly to unblock the POC.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com

From: Sam Liao <sam.liao@finventory.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@finventory.com
Date: 2027-05-21T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Edge VPN & peering performance qualification — post-demo recap

Thanks Marcus — appreciate the clear checklist. Quick answers from our infra side (ops@finventory.com is on cc):

- Network diagram: attaching our current VPC layout (I can put a cleaned diagram in the same Drive folder you linked). We currently peer to a partner colo and have a transit gateway for egress. Peering preferred if you can support direct VPC peering; otherwise VPN IPsec is acceptable as fallback.
- VPN: we run standard IPsec (AES-GCM), MTU 1436 (for IPsec overhead), no dynamic BGP on the current VPN (static routes today). We can stand up a BGP session if you need it.
- Firewall/proxies: no application-layer proxy in the streaming path; we do have an egress NAT gateway and optional TLS-inspecting appliances (can be bypassed for test).
- Egress: static NAT via a small set of IPs is doable for the test window; production will need a stable egress solution.
- Throughput: our baseline VPN nodes are 1 Gbps each; we can provision extra throughput for the test. Concurrency: we routinely handle 400–600 concurrent TLS sessions across the cluster; single-tunnel limits may apply.

We can support the validation next Friday morning Pacific (2027-05-28 08:30–11:30 PT). Ops suggests the following test window: 2027-05-28 09:00 PT for the initial run. Please confirm and provide the runbook/ports.

Sam
Sam Liao
Infra Lead, Finventory Inc.
sam.liao@finventory.com

Subject: Re: Edge VPN & peering performance qualification — internal next steps

Looping in a short internal plan based on Sam's reply.

Plan (internal):
- Marcus: confirm the exact static egress IP set and provide them the allowlist for the Private nodes.
- Dev: prepare rdw-perf-client script variations (streaming small frames, full-response bursts, p95/p99 telemetry) and a short PCAP checklist (we'll collect a few minutes of traffic during the run). Attach rdw-test-plan.pdf as the canonical runbook.
- Ops: provision a 3-node dedicated test pool (same model config as the POC) and expose telemetry (per-token latency, socket level metrics, and connection handshakes).

Notes for test config:
- Use TCP keepalives and HTTP/2 streaming (we will exercise both streaming and chunked responses)
- Start with 100 concurrent streams, ramp 50 every 2 minutes to 400, hold 5 minutes at target levels
- Validate MTU behaviour (1436) and check for fragmentation – if we see fragmentation we will lower TLS record sizes in the client
- Collect packet loss/jitter stats and compare with application-level p99 latencies

I'll drop rdw-test-plan.pdf in the Drive link and schedule a internal pre-call with Dev + our infra team tomorrow to finalize the runbook. Marcus — I'll let you manage the customer coordination.

—Stephanie

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Sam Liao <sam.liao@finventory.com>

Subject: Re: Edge VPN & peering performance qualification — scheduling & runbook link

All — thanks. Quick concrete steps from engineering and confirms for the 2027-05-28 09:00 PT test window that Sam proposed. I built an initial script and small checklist; sharing the essentials here and I uploaded the full artifacts to the Drive link (https://drive.google.com/finventory/perf-plan).

Quick runbook excerpt (will be in rdw-test-plan.pdf):
- Pre-test (T-48h): exchange allowlist IPs and open these ports: 443 (HTTPS gRPC/HTTP2), 2200 (optional SSH for debug). Confirm MTU 1436 on the tunnel.
- Test phases:
  1) Connectivity smoke (5 min): single streaming session, capture TLS handshake, verify no middlebox TLS termination.
  2) Latency baseline (10 min): 10 concurrent streams at 1 req/s to capture cold/warm token behaviour.
  3) Ramp test (25 min): start 100 concurrent streams, ramp +50 every 2 min to 400, hold each level 5 min. Observe per-token latency and p95/p99.
  4) Burst test (10 min): 500 concurrent short-lived requests (burst) and measure tail latency/failed connections.

- Measurement points: per-token breakouts (initial token vs continuation tokens), socket open time, TLS handshake time, and packet-level stats (loss/jitter). We're shipping client telemetry via StatsD and a short pcapture on both ends (pcap size capped to 20MB for handoff).

Commands (example):
rdw-perf-client --target https://private.redwood.internal --mode streaming --concurrency 200 --ramp 50 --duration 1800 --out statsd://rdw-internal:8125

Attachments uploaded: rdw_perf_script.sh (script wrapper), vpn-mtu-check.txt (utility to confirm MTU and fragmentation), rdw-test-plan.pdf.

Action owners & deadlines:
- Marcus: confirm allowlist & final customer contact (by 2027-05-24 EOD)
- Sam / Finventory ops: confirm static egress IPs and provision test window (confirm by 2027-05-24 EOD)
- Dev: provision test pool & finalize script (by 2027-05-26)
- Stephanie: run internal pre-call and validate observability dashboards (by 2027-05-26)

I'll be on the test call 05/28 09:00 PT. If anything changes, reply-all and we'll adjust.

—Dev
